ability.en: the power or skill to do something
ability.ex: Her ability to stay calm helped the team.

across.en: in many places or parts of

advocates.ex: The group advocates cleaner public transport.

age.ex: She started school at the age of four.

ageism.ex: Ageism can stop older people finding jobs.

alone.ex: He walked home alone after the party.

also.ex: She speaks French and also Spanish.

anticipate.ex: We anticipate heavy traffic this weekend.

example.en: Shops anticipate a busy Christmas season this year.
example.zh: 商店預期今年聖誕季會很忙碌。

note.usage: 接 that 子句或名詞/動名詞：anticipate that…, anticipate demand；名詞 anticipation。

noteEs.exampleTr: Las tiendas prevén una temporada navideña con mucho trabajo este año.
noteEs.usage: Se usa anticipate that… o anticipate demand; sustantivo anticipation.

noteHi.exampleTr: दुकानों को इस साल व्यस्त क्रिसमस सीज़न की उम्मीद है।
noteHi.meaning: अनुमान लगाना; किसी बात के होने की उम्मीद करना।
noteHi.usage: anticipate that… या anticipate demand; संज्ञा anticipation।

noteJa.exampleTr: 店は今年、忙しいクリスマスシーズンを見込んでいる。
noteJa.meaning: 予期する；起こると予想する。
noteJa.usage: anticipate that…、anticipate demand の形。名詞は anticipation。

noteKo.exampleTr: 상점들은 올해 바쁜 크리스마스 시즌을 예상한다.
noteKo.usage: anticipate that…, anticipate demand 형태. 명사는 anticipation.

anxieties.ex: Exams cause anxieties for many students.

approach.en: a way of dealing with something
approach.ex: We need a new approach to teaching maths.

areas.ex: She works in different areas of science.

argues.ex: The article argues that cities need more trees.

as.en: used to compare, give reasons or roles

asked.ex: The teacher asked us about our weekend.

at.en: in or near a place or time

authors.ex: The authors spent two years on the book.

average.ex: The average price of a house rose again.

based.en: based on: using as the starting point
based.ex: The film is based on a true story.

be.en: to exist or have a quality

become.ex: The town has become very popular with tourists.

benefit.ex: One benefit of cycling is better health.

benefits.ex: The job has many benefits, like free lunch.

biggest.ex: The biggest problem is the cost.

bit.ex: It is a bit cold today.

body.ex: A new body will check food safety.

born.ex: My brother was born in March.

bring.ex: The new factory will bring many jobs.

budgets.ex: Families are watching their budgets carefully.

burden.ex: High rent is a heavy burden for young workers.

example.en: She never wanted to be a burden on her children.
example.zh: 她從不想成為孩子們的負擔。

note.meaning: 負擔；沉重的責任或成本。
note.usage: 常見 a burden on sb；be seen as a burden；ease the burden。

noteEn.meaning: a heavy duty or cost that is hard to deal with.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'a burden on someone', 'ease the burden'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Ella nunca quiso ser una carga para sus hijos.
noteEs.usage: Se usa a burden on sb; ease the burden.

noteHi.exampleTr: वह कभी अपने बच्चों पर बोझ नहीं बनना चाहती थी।
noteHi.usage: a burden on sb; ease the burden आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 彼女は子どもたちの負担には決してなりたくなかった。
noteJa.usage: a burden on 人、ease the burden の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그녀는 자녀들에게 짐이 되고 싶지 않았다.
noteKo.usage: a burden on 사람, ease the burden 형태가 흔하다.

called.ex: Their new song is called Morning Light.

calls.ex: The report calls for more nurses.

care.en: help given to sick or old people
care.ex: Older people need good care at home.

centred.ex: The talk centred on climate change.

chance.ex: This trip is a chance to learn French.

changes.ex: The town has seen many changes recently.

charities.en: groups that help people in need
charities.ex: She gives money to two charities each month.

children.ex: The children played in the park.

citizen.en: a person who lives in a country
citizen.ex: Every citizen can vote at eighteen.

cognitive.ex: Puzzles help keep cognitive skills strong.

example.en: Puzzles may help slow cognitive decline in older people.
example.zh: 拼圖可能有助於減緩老年人的認知衰退。

note.meaning: 認知的；與思考、記憶、理解有關的。

noteEs.exampleTr: Los rompecabezas pueden frenar el deterioro cognitivo en los mayores.
noteEs.meaning: cognitivo; relacionado con pensar, recordar y entender.

noteHi.exampleTr: पहेलियाँ बुज़ुर्गों में संज्ञानात्मक गिरावट धीमी कर सकती हैं।
noteHi.meaning: संज्ञानात्मक; सोचने, याद रखने और समझने से जुड़ा।

noteJa.exampleTr: パズルは高齢者の認知機能の低下を遅らせるかもしれない。
noteJa.meaning: 認知の；思考・記憶・理解に関する。

noteKo.exampleTr: 퍼즐은 노인의 인지 능력 저하를 늦추는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.

commissioned.en: officially asked someone to do work
commissioned.ex: The council commissioned a new statue.

example.en: The council commissioned a study on local traffic.
example.zh: 市議會委託進行一項地方交通研究。

note.meaning: 委託（製作）；正式下令並出資進行報告或研究。
note.usage: 此處為動詞，常用 commission a report/study；被動 be commissioned by。

noteEn.meaning: to ask and pay someone to make a report or study.

noteEs.exampleTr: El ayuntamiento encargó un estudio sobre el tráfico local.
noteEs.meaning: encargar; pedir y pagar un informe o estudio.
noteEs.usage: Aquí es verbo: commission a report; pasiva be commissioned by.

noteHi.exampleTr: परिषद ने स्थानीय यातायात पर एक अध्ययन करवाया।
noteHi.meaning: किसी रिपोर्ट या अध्ययन को आदेश देकर और भुगतान करके करवाना।
noteHi.usage: यहाँ क्रिया: commission a report; passive: be commissioned by।

noteJa.exampleTr: 市議会は地域の交通に関する調査を委託した。
noteJa.meaning: 委託する；報告書や研究を依頼して作らせる。
noteJa.usage: ここでは動詞。commission a report、be commissioned by の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 시의회는 지역 교통에 관한 연구를 의뢰했다.
noteKo.meaning: 의뢰하다; 보고서나 연구를 맡겨 만들게 하다.
noteKo.usage: 여기서는 동사. commission a report, be commissioned by 형태가 흔하다.

community.ex: The community built a new playground.

compiled.ex: She compiled a list of useful phrases.

comprehensive.en: including all or nearly all parts
comprehensive.ex: The guide gives a comprehensive list of local services.

example.en: The government promised a comprehensive review of the health service.
example.zh: 政府承諾對醫療服務進行全面檢討。

note.meaning: 全面的；涵蓋所有方面的。
note.usage: 常用 a comprehensive strategy/review/plan；副詞 comprehensively。

noteEn.meaning: including all or nearly all parts of something.

noteEs.exampleTr: El gobierno prometió una revisión integral del servicio de salud.
noteEs.meaning: integral; que abarca todos los aspectos.

noteHi.exampleTr: सरकार ने स्वास्थ्य सेवा की व्यापक समीक्षा का वादा किया।
noteHi.meaning: व्यापक; सभी पहलुओं को शामिल करने वाला।

noteJa.exampleTr: 政府は医療サービスの包括的な見直しを約束した。
noteJa.meaning: 包括的な；すべての面を含む。
noteJa.usage: a comprehensive strategy/review/plan の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 정부는 의료 서비스에 대한 포괄적인 검토를 약속했다.

concern.ex: There is growing concern about rising rents.

concerned.ex: Parents are concerned about screen time.

concludes.ex: The study concludes that sleep helps memory.

consequences.ex: Bad sleep has serious consequences for health.

consequently.ex: It rained all day; consequently, the match was cancelled.

considerable.ex: The project needs a considerable amount of money.

contends.ex: The author contends that cities need more trees.

coordinate.en: to organise people or parts to work together

coordinated.ex: The event was coordinated by students.

cork.en: a city in the south of Ireland
cork.ja: コーク（アイルランドの都市）

cost.en: to need an amount of money
cost.ex: A new bike can cost a lot.

country.en: a nation with its own government

course.en: the way something develops over time
course.ex: The project is on course to finish early.
course.zh: 進程（on course：可望；life course：人生歷程）

cradle-to-grave.es: de la cuna a la tumba
cradle-to-grave.ex: The country offers cradle-to-grave health care.
cradle-to-grave.ja: ゆりかごから墓場までの
cradle-to-grave.zh: 從搖籃到墳墓的；終身的

crucially.ex: Crucially, the new drug has few side effects.
crucially.ja: 決定的に；重要なことに

currently.ex: She is currently living in Cork.

declining.ex: He worries about his declining eyesight.

dedicated.ex: The hospital has a dedicated children's ward.

demand.en: the need or wish for a service

designed.en: planned or made in a certain way
designed.ex: This course is designed for beginners.
designed.ja: 〜するよう作られた；意図された

divided.ex: The class was divided into groups.

doctors.en: people trained to treat sick people

drawing.ex: Drawing on her own life, she wrote a novel.

draws.ex: The film draws on real events.

economic.en: related to money and the economy

effects.ex: Coffee has strong effects on sleep.

estimates.en: makes a careful guess about a number
estimates.ex: The bank estimates that prices will rise.

existing.ex: We will improve the existing road.

expectancy.en: in 'life expectancy': how long people live
expectancy.ex: Life expectancy has risen in many countries.

expenditure.en: money spent, often by a government
expenditure.ex: Public expenditure on health keeps rising.

example.en: Public expenditure on housing rose sharply last year.
example.zh: 去年公共住房支出大幅增加。

note.meaning: 支出；（尤指政府或機構的）花費總額。
note.usage: 正式用語；常用 public/government expenditure、expenditure on sth。

noteEn.meaning: money spent, especially by a government.

noteEs.exampleTr: El gasto público en vivienda subió mucho el año pasado.
noteEs.meaning: gasto; dinero que gasta sobre todo el Estado.
noteEs.usage: Formal; public expenditure, expenditure on sth.

noteHi.exampleTr: पिछले साल आवास पर सार्वजनिक व्यय तेज़ी से बढ़ा।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक; public expenditure, expenditure on sth आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 昨年、住宅への公共支出が急増した。
noteJa.meaning: 支出；特に政府や組織の出費。
noteJa.usage: 硬い語。public expenditure、expenditure on ~ の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 작년 주택 부문 공공 지출이 크게 늘었다.
noteKo.usage: 격식어. public expenditure, expenditure on ~ 형태가 흔하다.

expert.en: from or by people with special knowledge
expert.ex: She gave expert advice on money.

experts.ex: Experts say the river is safe.

expressed.ex: Many people expressed concern about the plan.

far-reaching.en: having a big effect on many things
far-reaching.ex: The law will have far-reaching effects.

finances.en: money that a government or person has
finances.ex: The war hurt the country's finances.

flourish.en: to grow and do very well
flourish.ex: Children flourish when they feel safe at home.

for.en: used to show purpose or who gets something

foremost.ex: Safety is our foremost concern on the road.

foresee.en: to expect something before it happens
foresee.ex: Nobody could foresee such a big change.

collocations: as far as I can foresee

example.en: Few experts foresaw such a rapid rise in prices.
example.zh: 很少專家預見到價格會如此快速上漲。

note.meaning: 預見；事先料到將來會發生的事。
note.usage: 不規則動詞 foresee–foresaw–foreseen；常用 foresee problems/difficulties。

noteEn.meaning: to know or expect something before it happens.

noteEs.exampleTr: Pocos expertos previeron una subida tan rápida de los precios.
noteEs.meaning: prever; saber de antemano lo que pasará.

noteHi.exampleTr: कुछ ही विशेषज्ञों ने कीमतों में इतनी तेज़ बढ़ोतरी का अनुमान लगाया था।
noteHi.meaning: पूर्वानुमान करना; भविष्य में होने वाली बात पहले से देख लेना।
noteHi.usage: अनियमित क्रिया foresee–foresaw–foreseen; foresee problems आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 物価がこれほど急上昇すると予見した専門家は少なかった。
noteJa.meaning: 予見する；将来起こることを前もって見通す。
noteJa.usage: 不規則動詞 foresee–foresaw–foreseen。foresee problems の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 가격이 이렇게 빨리 오를 것을 예견한 전문가는 거의 없었다.
noteKo.meaning: 예견하다; 앞으로 일어날 일을 미리 내다보다.
noteKo.usage: 불규칙 동사 foresee–foresaw–foreseen. foresee problems 형태가 흔하다.

forfeiting.en: losing something, often as a result
forfeiting.ex: He risked forfeiting his place by arriving late.

foundation.en: an organisation that gives money to good causes

fragmented.ex: The fragmented system makes care hard to find.

example.en: Mental health care in the region is badly fragmented.
example.zh: 該地區的心理健康照護非常分散零碎。

note.meaning: 零碎的；分散而缺乏統一協調的。
note.usage: 常形容制度或政策：a fragmented system/approach；be fragmented across。

noteEn.meaning: split into parts that do not work well together.

noteEs.exampleTr: La atención de salud mental en la región está muy fragmentada.
noteEs.usage: Se usa con sistemas o políticas: a fragmented system; fragmented across.

noteHi.exampleTr: क्षेत्र में मानसिक स्वास्थ्य सेवा बहुत बिखरी हुई है।
noteHi.meaning: खंडित; बिखरा हुआ, बिना एकीकृत समन्वय के।
noteHi.usage: व्यवस्था/नीति के लिए: a fragmented system; fragmented across।

noteJa.exampleTr: その地域の精神医療はひどくばらばらだ。
noteJa.meaning: 断片的な；ばらばらで統一されていない。
noteJa.usage: 制度や政策に使う：a fragmented system、fragmented across。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 지역의 정신 건강 서비스는 매우 분산되어 있다.
noteKo.usage: 제도나 정책에 쓴다: a fragmented system, fragmented across.

frailty.en: being physically weak, especially when old
frailty.ex: Regular exercise can delay frailty in old age.

fully.ex: The new road is not fully open yet.

geared.en: designed or arranged for a purpose
geared.ex: The course is geared towards beginners.

generations.en: groups of people born around the same time
generations.ex: Three generations live in the same house.

gives.ex: My grandmother gives money to the local church.

good.ex: This is a good place to study.

government.en: the group of people who run a country
government.ex: The government will build new schools.

group.ex: A local group cleans the beach every month.

grow.ex: Children grow up very fast these days.

growing.ex: There is a growing need for nurses.

health.en: the condition of your body and mind
health.ex: Walking every day is good for your health.

healthcare.en: services that look after people's health

heavy.en: large in amount; hard to bear

held.ex: The club held a party last night.

however.ex: The test was hard; however, everyone passed.

idea.ex: That is a great idea for a party.

ill-equipped.en: not having what is needed to deal with something
ill-equipped.ex: The small hospital was ill-equipped for the crisis.

impairment.en: damage that stops something working well
impairment.ex: Hearing impairment is common in older people.

example.en: Hearing impairment is common among older adults.
example.zh: 聽力障礙在年長者中很常見。

note.meaning: 損傷；功能（身體或心智）的減弱或障礙。
note.usage: 常用 cognitive/visual/hearing impairment；動詞 impair。

noteEn.meaning: when part of the body or mind does not work well.

noteEs.exampleTr: La pérdida auditiva es común entre las personas mayores.
noteEs.meaning: deterioro; pérdida de una función física o mental.
noteEs.usage: Se usa cognitive/visual/hearing impairment; verbo impair.

noteHi.exampleTr: बुज़ुर्गों में सुनने की क्षमता में कमी आम है।
noteHi.meaning: क्षति; शारीरिक या मानसिक क्षमता में कमी।
noteHi.usage: cognitive/visual/hearing impairment आम है; क्रिया impair।

noteJa.exampleTr: 聴覚障害は高齢者によく見られる。
noteJa.meaning: 障害；身体や心の機能の低下。
noteJa.usage: cognitive/visual/hearing impairment の形が多い。動詞は impair。

noteKo.usage: cognitive/visual/hearing impairment 형태가 흔하다. 동사는 impair.

implications.ex: The new law has serious implications for farmers.

example.en: The new law has serious implications for small farms.
example.zh: 新法律對小型農場有重大影響。

note.usage: 常用複數 implications for sth；serious/far-reaching implications。

noteEn.meaning: a possible effect or result of something.

noteEs.exampleTr: La nueva ley tiene serias implicaciones para las pequeñas granjas.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir en plural: implications for sth; serious implications.

noteHi.exampleTr: नए क़ानून का छोटे खेतों पर गंभीर प्रभाव पड़ेगा।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर बहुवचन: implications for sth; serious implications।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい法律は小規模農場に深刻な影響を及ぼす。
noteJa.meaning: （将来の）影響；起こりうる結果。
noteJa.usage: 複数形 implications for ~ の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 법은 소규모 농장에 심각한 영향을 미친다.
noteKo.meaning: 영향; 앞으로 생길 수 있는 결과.
noteKo.usage: 보통 복수형 implications for ~ 형태로 쓴다.

impose.en: to force something unwelcome on someone
impose.ex: The new tax will impose costs on small shops.

in.en: inside; at a place or time

increased.ex: Increased traffic has made the roads busy.

independence.en: being able to live without help

institute.en: an organisation for research or a special purpose
institute.ex: He works at a medical research institute.

interviews.en: meetings where people are asked questions
interviews.ex: The reporter did interviews with local farmers.

isolation.en: being alone, without contact with others
isolation.ex: Isolation can harm older people's health.

laments.ex: The writer laments the loss of local shops.

life.en: the time a person is alive
life.ex: She had a long and happy life.

lifespans.ex: Pets have shorter lifespans than people.

likely.ex: It is likely to rain tomorrow.

live.en: to stay alive; to have a home
live.ex: Many people now live past ninety.

lives.ex: Doctors save many lives every day.

living.ex: Living alone can be hard for older people.

long.en: lasting a great amount of time
long.ex: We had a long walk by the river.

longer.ex: The days get longer in spring.

longevity.ex: Good food and exercise may help longevity.

example.en: Good diet and exercise are linked to longevity.
example.zh: 良好的飲食與運動和長壽有關。

note.usage: 不可數名詞，偏正式；常用 increased longevity、the secret of longevity。

noteEs.exampleTr: La buena alimentación y el ejercicio están ligados a la longevidad.
noteEs.usage: Sustantivo formal e incontable; increased longevity.

noteHi.exampleTr: अच्छा आहार और व्यायाम दीर्घायु से जुड़े हैं।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक, अगणनीय संज्ञा; increased longevity आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 良い食事と運動は長寿と関係がある。
noteJa.usage: やや硬い不可算名詞。increased longevity の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 좋은 식단과 운동은 장수와 관련이 있다.
noteKo.usage: 격식 있는 불가산 명사. increased longevity 형태가 흔하다.

losing.ex: He is afraid of losing his job.

loss.en: the fact of no longer having something
loss.ex: The loss of her keys made her late.

lot.ex: We have a lot of homework today.

majority.en: more than half of a group
majority.ex: The majority of students passed the test.

meetings.en: events where people meet to talk
meetings.ex: We have two meetings every Monday.

members.en: people who belong to a family

memory.ex: My grandmother has a very good memory.

men.ex: Men and women joined the walk.

mental.ex: Puzzles keep your mental skills sharp.

moment.ex: She is busy at the moment.

money.en: what you use to buy things
money.ex: I saved money for a new bike.

more.en: a larger amount; to a greater degree

most.ex: She was most worried about her exams.

mounting.ex: There is mounting worry about rising prices.

national.ex: The national team won the match.

nationally.ex: The show is broadcast nationally every Friday.
nationally.zh: 全國性地（nationally representative：具全國代表性）

need.ex: You need a ticket to enter.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.

new.ex: She bought a new coat for winter.

not.ex: I am not hungry right now.

notable.ex: The new bridge is a notable success.

old.ex: My old neighbour walks every morning.

on.en: used for days, topics and places

opportunity.en: a chance to do something good
opportunity.ex: This job is a great opportunity for her.

overseen.ex: The project was overseen by a senior engineer.

page.en: one side of a sheet in a book

paid.ex: The trip was paid for by the school.

particular.ex: She showed a particular interest in music.

pensions.en: money paid to people after they stop work
pensions.ex: Older people depend on their pensions.

people.ex: Many people came to the concert.

perceived.en: seen or understood in a certain way
perceived.ex: He is perceived as a strong leader.

physical.ex: Physical exercise is good for your heart.

placing.ex: Rising rent is placing pressure on families.
placing.zh: placing a strain on：對…造成壓力

plan.en: to decide what to do in the future
plan.ex: We plan to visit Cork next summer.

policy.ex: The new policy helps first-time buyers.

polling.ex: Polling shows most people support the plan.

poor.ex: Poor sleep can make you tired all day.

potential.ex: We discussed potential problems with the plan.

paragraphs: A new report says one in three children born in Ireland today may live to 100.
Now, people in Ireland live for about 83 years on average. Women live a bit longer than men.
The report says Ireland is not ready for this. More old people will need doctors and pensions. This will cost the State a lot of money.
People were asked about a very long life. They worry about their health, their memory and living alone. But they also like the idea of seeing their family grow up.
The writers want one public body to plan for longer lives. They say a long life can be a good thing.

One in three children born in Ireland today is likely to live to 100, according to a new report. The report, called The 100-Year Lives Project, was paid for by Community Foundation Ireland, a group that gives money to charities.

At the moment, the average life expectancy in Ireland is 82.9 years: 84.6 for women and 81.3 for men. The writers say Ireland is not ready for the changes that longer lives will bring. More people will need health care and State pensions, and this will put pressure on Government budgets.

The report spoke to 16 experts and held meetings with people in Dublin, Cork and Mullingar. Many people said their biggest worries about living to 100 were poor health (84%), memory problems (83%) and losing their independence (82%). But 86% said a good thing would be seeing younger family members grow up.
The writers want a national body to plan for longer lives. They say people should see a long life as a chance, not a problem.
One in three children born in Ireland today can expect to reach 100, according to a new report which warns that the country is not fully prepared for the effects of longer lives.

The 98-page study, The 100-Year Lives Project, was commissioned by Community Foundation Ireland and written by social psychologist Karen Hand and strategy specialist Carolyn Ogdens. It draws on interviews with 16 experts, public workshops in Dublin, Cork and Mullingar, and national polling. Average life expectancy currently stands at 82.9 years.

The authors predict that rising demand for healthcare and State pensions will put heavy pressure on public finances. Those surveyed were most concerned about physical health (84%), declining mental ability (83%) and losing their independence (82%), although many also saw benefits, such as watching younger relatives grow up (86%).

The report argues that Irish policy is still designed for shorter lives and is divided between separate areas such as health and pensions. It recommends a dedicated national body to coordinate planning and urges people to treat longevity as an opportunity rather than a burden.
A third of children born in Ireland today are on course to become centenarians, yet the country is ill-equipped for the far-reaching consequences of longer lifespans, a new report contends.

Commissioned by Community Foundation Ireland, The 100-Year Lives Project was compiled by social psychologist Karen Hand and strategist Carolyn Ogdens, drawing on 16 expert interviews, citizen workshops and nationally representative polling.

The authors foresee mounting demand for healthcare and State pensions placing a severe strain on the public purse. Respondents' foremost anxieties centred on physical frailty (84%), cognitive impairment (83%) and forfeiting their independence (82%), while isolation and ageism weighed on about two-thirds. On the upside, 86% relished the prospect of seeing younger generations flourish.

Crucially, the report laments that Irish policy remains geared towards a shorter life and is fragmented across ageing, health and pensions. It advocates a 'cradle-to-grave' approach, overseen by a dedicated institute, and calls for longevity to be reframed as an opportunity rather than a burden.

A recent report estimates that one third of children born in Ireland today will live to the age of 100. However, it concludes that the country is insufficiently prepared for the substantial social and economic implications of increased longevity.

The study, commissioned by Community Foundation Ireland, was based on interviews with 16 experts, citizen workshops and nationally representative surveys. At present, average life expectancy in Ireland is 82.9 years.

The authors anticipate that growing demand for healthcare and State pensions will impose considerable pressure on public expenditure. Respondents expressed particular concern regarding physical health (84%), cognitive impairment (83%) and the potential loss of independence (82%). Nevertheless, a significant majority (86%) regarded witnessing younger family members mature as a notable benefit.

The report contends that existing policy remains fragmented and is predicated on a shorter life course. Consequently, it recommends a comprehensive 'cradle-to-grave' strategy, coordinated by a dedicated institute, and argues that longevity should be perceived as an opportunity rather than a burden.
